paper.title: Incomplete gamma functions with negative arguments (Algorithm 926)

stack: Fortran 90 (TOMS 926 archive 926.zip: Fortran/Src/in_gamma_sequence.f90, driver Fortran/Driver/in_gamma_test.f90, shipped Maple data in_gamma_test.dat)

claim.text: Summary of in_gamma_test, menu choice 2 (compare with the shipped Maple data), summary mode 1: the count of evaluations with 53 correct binary digits is 30540 (tol +/-100), out of 51051 evaluations in total (exact). Registered by scout (queue entry); the value is the shipped reference RES, not a verified paper table (ACM refuses the article from this sandbox).

attempt: Original attempt (G1) succeeded as documented: the authors' manual gives the gfortran flags `-c -std=f2003 -cpp` for in_gamma_sequence.f90 (Doc/manual.tex). The driver was compiled with the same flags against that module and run with its menu answered 2 then 1 (summary). Output matches the shipped RES: 'A total of 51051 evaluations were performed.' and '53 correct digits : 30540 occurrences (59.8225%)', identical in every line of the summary. No source file was changed; the gfortran warning 'Illegal preprocessor directive' is about the `#endif` lines, which -cpp handles. Compiler gfortran 16.2.0 (conda-forge).
